about: Rows as DB.lua writes them and the helper must carry them (tools/gen-fixtures.lua): ts|char|questID|tier|slot|ladder|rung|move|kind|reps|seconds|outcome|flags; a pose's flow row carries its answer to "How close to the goal pose?" in reps (codes.mark, 0 none; since 2026-10-09), a hold row of the wall sit, the core, the side plank or the L-sit its answer to "Could you have held longer?" in reps (codes.longer, 0 not asked; since slice 52, 2026-10-23), a load row (codes.kind load, since 2026-10-09) the weight of the set row after it in tenths of a kg, and since 2026-10-16 a cardio move row the player's answer after it in flags bits 14-15 (answer_shift): on a counted set codes.answer slipped for "Form slipped" and, since slice 53, notAllOut for "Not all out" (0 Yes, to the end, its count in reps, 0 none), on a steady move its answer to "Did you keep that pace to the end?" (codes.pace, 0 none), and since slice 48's double-check a rep or hold row of a match pump's warm move codes.set warm in the same bits (its easy set, which the fold counts as no fresh set: DB.lua applyRow); a mastered row (codes.kind mastered) a step mastered, its ladder and rung, reps 0, or reps 7 (the rung rows' undo cause, 2026-10-17) a /qp undo's that takes back the mastered row of its character on that ladder and step that it names, both then folding as never written (DB.lua undone, applyRow), as a rung undo row takes back the rung row of its character on its ladder it names: since 2026-10-19 an undo names the row it reverses by that row's ts in its questID and pairs with it alone (the grammar's named undo), and one with questID 0 (every undo before) pairs with the latest such row before it; a trim that folds that row into the save's baseline ahead of its undo keeps the pair (the baseline carries the pairing at its edge, and the other open step rows of its last correct_days game days, kept: DB.lua ns.Trim, slice 44, 2026-10-19); since slice 44 (2026-10-18) a correction row and a correction's load row carry their round in outcome (the grammar's last three rows: Correct a count, DB.lua ns.CorrectionBeats)

catchup.about: a catch-up pump from the phone: each move pays the oldest owed row of the move it names (the plain moves, then every all-out window, oldest first, each paid with reps 1: both finishers; at most one until 2026-10-14), and a move nothing owes writes no row; a closing move owed before 2026-10-15 (reps 2, under the id of the steady form that led it) is an all-out window of the move it names, the jumping jacks, whose finisher rung is above the cardio rung, so it is held: the sheet painted then holds it back (held), the helper leaves it out of what a catch-up can pay, and it stays owed; the loaded move's count (its set, since 2026-10-12) is written as the game's own catch-up writes it, at the moment it was saved: the load row, the set row past the record and the rung row it brought, which the fold reads as the record, its weight and the climb

catchup_named.about: a later catch-up from the phone whose moves name the owed rows they were dosed from (ts), each named row taken first while it is still owed, then the oldest free row of each move left: the first push-up move names a row the player skipped in the game meanwhile, so the helper drops its count and pays the oldest push-up set still free, the third, done; the second names the second row, which it pays with its count (the push-ups' record) though the first move fell back to a newer row; the old closing move's window rides now (the cardio rung climbed past its form's finisher rung), the window of the jumping jacks it names alone, a counted set written as their row with the count, the counted bit and count_s, its paid row clearing the owed one; the fold reads the counts as the records and owes nothing after

feedback.about: the feedback window's Send (contract/feedback-api.yaml, GameFeedback): the message, with the numbers the window counted (a pump finished, one banked, a move stopped early, one taken as the easier version), in the profile event's chunk layout with its own serial, painted once in the blobs lane; message is what the frames carry, read back from them, which the helper posts with source game

message.text: The pumps after a quest hub are great.

grammar.about: a record, typed and confirmed on a first try (flags above 255)
a pain flag (the joint id in move)
a cardio move stopped for feeling unwell
a pump banked for feeling unwell
a reset (/qp reset all): the new save's first row
a start rung after the reset

a ladder pose held its whole time on its family's ladder and rung, as written before 2026-10-09's ask (no mark bit: practice, no day toward the family's unlock since 2026-10-31, the family's attempt alone; read as Good on its main pose from 2026-10-26 and as Perfect until then, slice 21)
an app row: a record typed in the app's own pump, sent by the phone with the app bit (11) and the phone's (7), char 0; it never pays or owes an unfinished move (DB.lua applyRow)

a load row (kind load, 2026-10-09): the weight one set of a loaded move was done with, 11 kg as 110 tenths of a kg in reps, written just before its set row with that row's ts, char, questID, tier, slot, ladder, rung and move, seconds and outcome 0 and the set row's source bits in flags; the fold reads the set with it (a correction's load row corrects the weight, below; 0 takes it off), and an older reader skips it
its set row: 16 reps of the one-arm row with 11 kg

a correction row (kind correction; its round since slice 44, 2026-10-18): it names its set by that row's ts, questID, slot and move (the fold reads it as the move that took a merged one), repeats its tier, ladder and rung, and carries the count the set should have had, a rep or counted set's in reps, a hold's seconds in seconds, a pose's answer to "How close to the goal pose?" in reps (codes.mark), and its round in outcome: one more than the highest round of that set (a correction's or a load row's) its writer held, at most 255, 0 on a row from before the rounds (/qp undo's); its char and source bits are its writer's: here the phone's, 14 reps of the one-arm row, round 1

a correction's load row: the weight the set should have had (12 kg as 120 tenths, 0 none), written by Correct a count just before its correction row where the weight changes (or where the set's own side reads another weight than the one it reads with now, since 2026-10-19), with the correction's round in outcome and its writer's char and source bits (the game's here: char 1, none)

the game's correction row after it: 15 reps, round 2. Of the rows naming one set every fold reads the one of the highest round, of two alike the smaller value (a load row's the lower weight), of rows of round 0 the last in its log (DB.lua ns.CorrectionBeats): the set reads 15 reps with 12 kg everywhere; rung and mastered rows a correction asks again (and their undo rows) carry the set's char and the time they were written
a climb an app wrote (character 0, a phone's: no bits as the phone keeps it), push to rung 6
a later climb of the same character from the watch (the app and watch bits), push to rung 7, which reaches the phone only after the undo below

the undo of the first climb (codes.kind rung, reps 7, the undo cause; rung the rung its ladder goes back to), written by the phone's correction of the set that made it, naming the row it reverses by that row's ts in questID (2026-10-19): every fold pairs it with that row alone, the newest rung row of its character on its ladder at that ts and at another rung, wherever it stands, so the watch's climb stands (push at rung 7); an undo with questID 0 (every undo before 2026-10-19) pairs with the latest rung row of its character on that ladder before it, which here would take the watch's climb back. A mastered undo names its mastered row alike

import.about: An export (DB.lua ns.Export) imported into a save whose characters number otherwise (slice 44's last review, 2026-10-19): the export's save has characters A and B (1 and 2), and a trim folded into its baseline B's first max set at its window's top, the climb it made, an owed move of B's, B's pause until resumed and B's set at the top the next game day, while the correction of the first set under the top and B's undo row taking the climb back stay in its ring (the export here carries those two alone); it is imported on B into a fresh save whose one character is B, so B is 1 and A 2 there. ns.Import takes an export's baseline into a save with no history of its own under that save's numbers, as the merge numbers the export's rows (characters by GUID): the characters' pauses (keyed by character), the owed rows and the edge (row texts) and the undo pairing at its edge (pairing.rungs keyed ladder:char and pairing.steps ladder:rung:char, each holding a row text, and pairing.kept, the other open step rows of the last correct_days game days to the edge a named undo may still name, row texts in time order: here B's start rung row; 2026-10-19). The ring's undo is one from before the named undo (questID 0), so it pairs with the latest rung row of its character. So the undo pairs with B's climb, as a fold of every row pairs it (the ladder keeps the day B's set reached its top: hi_days; an undo read unpaired, here against A's start rung row, resets it), B is the paused character and the owed move B's, and the helper's mirror after it (every row of the export's save, under the export's characters) brings no row the baseline folded (taken: the game rows it merged). Each: the export (its string, characters and ring), the save's characters before and after, the baseline's pairing, pauses, owed rows and edge after the import, and before (the fold of every row) and after (the save's fold after the import): the push ladder's rung and hi_days, the characters paused at `at` and the owed moves' characters

logout.about: logout at the second move's Ready view: the second and third moves are owed, dated at the pump's offered time
logout while the second move's count is typed: that move is the addon's own done row, the helper owes only the third

merge.about: The mirror's rows merged into a save (slice 26: one progression, the game's, the other installs' and the apps'), as ns.BindDB merges them: a reset made elsewhere first (ns.MirrorReset: a reset row newer than the save's own resets the save, kept as the backup, its characters and profiles kept), then ns.MergeMirror from the save's reset on (characters by GUID, each list's own order, the two lists by time, a row the save holds kept once by copies), folded by ns.Fold. An app row (flags bit 11 with exactly one device's bit: the phone's 7, the watch's 4 on its own pump, the computer's 12 on the desktop app's; char 0) moves the records, every clock, the pain flags, the felt-unwell lock, the focus and the rungs (a climb to a rung not above the ladder's rung now changes nothing, whichever side made it), but never the owed queue or the day's game counts (pumps, moves, records, banked; the app's own pumps, moves and records are counted beside them, day.app); the sheet counts its pump as a catch-up's (slice 27: its XP, stats and wins, a rung paid once at its first reach from any source, never paying or owing unfinished moves) and its Log names the pump; a catch-up (a device's bit, the phone's, the watch's or the computer's, no app bit) is the game's. Each case: the save (rows, chars by GUID, reset_at), the mirror (rows, chars), at (the probe's time), reset (a reset made elsewhere that reset the save) and backup_rows, the merged log and chars, taken (the mirror's rows merged, by source), and before and after: the anchor's record and goal (move 43, push rung 2), the push ladder's last set, its rung, best rung and hi_days (the days its top was reached at that rung), the pain flags, locked, focus, owed, the day's counts, the characters paused, the sheet's XP and its Log (source and device: codes.source, codes.device)

cases.about: a record typed in the app raises the game's record and its next goal
cases.name: app_record_raises_goal

cases.about: an app set on a ladder is that ladder's last set: the major move's clock and the fresh-set clock run from it
cases.name: app_set_is_last_set

cases.about: a pain flag set in the app flags the joint in the game
cases.name: app_pain_flags_joint

cases.about: an app pump's felt-unwell stop (its pump row banked for feeling unwell) locks the game until the next game day
cases.name: app_stop_locks_day

cases.about: the focus the app's row sets is the game's
cases.name: app_focus

cases.about: an app row never owes and never pays an unfinished move: its owed and banked move rows and a paid row that names the game's owed move leave the queue and the day's game counts as they were (its pump counts only in the app's beside them)
cases.name: app_never_owes

cases.about: the game's sheet counts an app pump as it counts a catch-up (slice 27: its XP, its stats and its wins) and its Log names each app pump with its device, the phone's, the watch's and the computer's own pump (slice 35: the desktop app's, 11|12), its moves with their counts
cases.name: sheet_counts_app_pump_log_names

cases.about: a catch-up the helper wrote for unfinished moves paid on the phone is the game's: it pays the owed move and its XP, and its Log entry names the phone
cases.name: catchup_log_names_device

cases.about: a catch-up the helper wrote for unfinished moves paid in the desktop app (slice 35: the computer's bit 12, no app bit) is the game's as the phone's is: it pays the owed move and its XP, and its Log entry names the computer
cases.name: catchup_log_names_computer

cases.about: a row the save holds already is kept once; two rows alike in the mirror's list (two sets in one second) stay two
cases.name: alike_twice_kept_once

cases.about: after /qp reset all an app row dated before the reset stays out; one after it counts
cases.name: app_before_reset_out

cases.about: a /qp reset all made in another install resets this save at the login: its rows from before the reset go (the save kept as the backup), its characters and profiles stay, and the mirror's rows from the reset on merge
cases.name: reset_elsewhere

cases.about: another install's characters by GUID: the mirror's character 2 (B) is not this save's 2 (C, met while the helper was off), so B joins as 3 and its rows and its pause move with it
cases.name: chars_by_guid

cases.about: the app and the game each climbed the push ladder to the next rung before they synced: the later climb (the game's) changes nothing, so the day the app's set reached the new rung's top still counts toward the rung after it; the rung was reached first in the app, so the app's climb pays it and the game's pays nothing (slice 27: the pay moves to the first reach, never lost)
cases.name: climbed_both_counts_kept

cases.about: the app climbed the push ladder two rungs while the game, not yet synced, climbed the first of them later: a climb to a rung below the ladder's rung now changes nothing, so the ladder keeps the app's rung
cases.name: climb_below_changes_nothing

cases.about: a rung climbed in the app is reached in the game and pays its climb there once (slice 27: the sheet counts an app pump as a catch-up's)
cases.name: app_climb_reached

cases.about: after a rung down in the game, the rung the app climbed stays reached (its colour is kept), and another install's climb back to it is Rekindled and pays nothing
cases.name: climb_back_rekindled

pump_done.about: a pump banked at its Ready view: its pump_done frame names the pump by its offered time (row_ts) and how it ended in the outcome byte, one of ended's codes, which the helper hands the phones as the command's ended (0, done, from an addon before slice 29)

reset.about: on the reset row the helper drops every row before it, and afterwards any row dated before it (a late catch-up for the deleted save)

setup.about: the setup word: cell 2's flags, bits 4-7 (setup in each frame's fields), in every frame since 2026-10-13; word's codes: present in every frame of an addon that paints it (0 from an older one: the helper cannot tell), check_again while the game's setup window asks for its Check again (on screen, or held back by a fight, a pump or a cinematic), helper_seen when the running load found QuestPump on the computer running, save_unread on a client that does not read its own save back (the Forever beta). From it the helper names Helper.step (contract/companion-api.yaml)

frames.name: the beta's first login without the helper: Check again on screen
Play without them: Your setup, no Check again
a client that reads its save back, the helper running: Check again on screen

unwell.about: a move stopped or a pump banked for feeling unwell locks every pump until the next game day at 04:00 (the day turns at 04:00 local time; this file is in UTC)
